title: UFO arrives in Milan: a new hybrid space combining food, music, and culture in the South of Prada neighborhood
excerpt: UFO – Unconventional Form of Opportunities opens at Via Orobia 26, a project of over 1.500 square meters that brings together bistros, music, events, publishing and creativity in one of the most transformed areas of Milan.
content:
Milan continues to change, and in the southern quadrant of the city, this transformation increasingly involves the creation of spaces capable of blending functions, audiences, and languages. It is in this context that UFO – Unconventional Form of Opportunities – arrives at Via Orobia 26 , a project spanning over 1.500 square meters that brings together restaurants, culture, music, communications, and events.

The location is no coincidence. UFO is located in the area dubbed South of Prada , a short walk from the Fondazione Prada and the Fondazione ICA Milano, in an area undergoing a process of progressive urban redevelopment and set to undergo further transformation with the development of the Scalo Romana railway line and the future Olympic Village. The project was also featured by Domus as an example of a new generation of Milanese spaces that transcend the traditional distinction between venue, cultural venue, and creative platform.

UFO was born with a decidedly transversal vocation. The gastronomic heart is UFO Bistrot, flanked by a lounge bar, a bocce ball area, and spaces for cultural programming. The food, according to descriptions published in Milanese guides, ranges from dishes designed for sharing to interpretations of Italian cuisine, in a more informal setting than a traditional restaurant. But the gastronomic component is only part of the project. In the large complex on Via Orobia, several creative realities coexist: Billboard Italy, Quip, podcast production studio founded by Selvaggia Lucarelli and Lorenzo Biagiarelli, Cuckoo Creative Studio, the corner of Frabs Magazine e SpaceDelicious, a company active in communications and events related to the food and beverage world. Their presence makes UFO something more than a new place to eat or drink: the idea is to create an environment where different activities can meet and spark new collaborations.

Completing the project is an events space of over 400 square meters , designed to be easily reconfigured and host a variety of events: from talks to presentations, performances to listening sessions, and even corporate events. The venue's cultural vocation was already evident during Milan Art Week 2025, when UFO hosted the MEGA Art Fair , along with performances and projects related to contemporary art.

The result is a particularly contemporary model of social interaction: during the day, the same location can function as a workplace and creative outlet, while later it transforms into a bistro, lounge, event space, or meeting place. It's a formula that reflects a broader shift in the geography of Milan's nightlife and culture, where increasingly, new venues don't have a single purpose but instead build hybrid experiences around diverse communities and interests.

The presence of bocce ball also contributes to UFO's character. Rather than focusing solely on the aesthetics of a contemporary venue, the project incorporates an element strongly rooted in Italian sociality and reinterprets it within a post-industrial context. The result is a courtyard that, as Vivimilano also described, combines outdoor seating, tables, lounge areas, and play areas, creating an informal atmosphere within a creative complex.

Behind UFO are, among others, Fabio Lucarelli and Claudio Larcher . The former is linked to Milanese projects involving the regeneration and conversion of spaces, while Larcher brings to the project a path that combines architecture, design, research, and education. Born in Milan and graduated in Architecture from the Polytechnic University, Larcher founded Modoloco Design Workshop in 2002 and has developed design and teaching activities in Italy and abroad over the years. NABA today names him Design Area Leader , confirming the role he continues to play in the Academy's design area.

UFO's story thus fits into that of a Milan that is progressively shifting its cultural center of gravity southward. Via Orobia and the Scalo Romana area have in recent years become an urban laboratory where contemporary art, design, new gastronomic formats, creative studios, and spaces dedicated to cultural production coexist. The presence of Fondazione Prada and ICA Milano has helped consolidate this identity, while new developments are adding further functions and opportunities for socializing.

The name UFO – Unconventional Form of Opportunities – epitomizes, at least in the project's intentions, this very goal: not to simply create another restaurant or a new event space, but a platform where food, music, design, publishing, and communication can converge. This venue thus attempts to convey, through its architecture and programming, one of the directions taken by contemporary Milan: fewer monofunctional spaces and more ecosystems capable of shifting identities throughout the day.

And in a city accustomed to transforming former industrial areas into new creative districts, UFO arrives precisely at the point where this metamorphosis is still underway. Not just a simple venue, then, but a new piece in the urban geography of South of Prada.
